From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1,2}=\pm 1,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 4\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1(x-1)(x-(-1))(x-(4\text{i}))(x-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =1(x-1)(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}+x-x-{1}^{2})({x}^{2}+4\text{i}x-4\text{i}x-(4\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-1)({x}^{2}+16) & = \\ {x}^{4}+16{x}^{2}-{x}^{2}-16 & = \\ {x}^{4}+15{x}^{2}-16 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{4}+15{x}^{2}-16.$
